result.summary: The landlord's reply "Yes please!" is a clear approval to send a contractor, so I recorded it against approval 54 with no amount. This ticket looks like a duplicate of ticket 95 (R/PM036-2), which has the same property, description, timestamps and landlord reply, and already has Keystone Services / Oliver Turner assigned. I did not assign a contractor here because the same job would be sent out twice. I've passed it to ops to confirm the duplicate and close or merge it.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 006 is a clear, unconditional approval (classify_reply: approve, unconditional 0.88), so I recorded it. The normal next step would be to assign a contractor. But ticket 95 has events 001–006 identical to this ticket, word for word and to the second, and it already has an assigned provider. Sending a contractor from ticket 97 would duplicate the job and could double-bill the landlord. Lessons #22 and #51 say to move an approved job forward with no further reply to the landlord. I followed them for the approval and stopped before assignment because of the duplicate.
